cards.text: Japan has picked three projects to store about 10 million tonnes of CO2 a year off Malaysia. No tonne has shipped, and the deal that would set long-term duties is unsigned.
cards.sub: The federal CCUS Act covers Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan, where two of the sites lie. Sarawak regulates the third under its own 2023 ordinance.
sources: METI/JOGMEC, Advanced CCS Projects selection, 28 Jun 2024: Northern Offshore Peninsular (~3 Mtpa), Offshore Sarawak (~1.9-2.9 Mtpa), Southern Offshore Peninsular (~5 Mtpa) [brief S7]
Petronas, 1 Apr 2026: no agreement signed with Japan; bilateral agreement needed (reported) [S15]; Ministry of Economy, 15 Sep 2026: meetings 'towards the finalisation of bilateral agreements' [S9a]

Act 870 s. 2 ('This Act shall apply to Peninsular Malaysia and the Federal Territory of Labuan') [S1a p. 8]; Sarawak Environment (Reduction of Greenhouse Gases Emission) Ordinance 2023, s. 3 and First Schedule [S8]

cards.h: On 23 Oct 2026 Petronas, TotalEnergies and Mitsui signed a joint venture for a CO2 storage hub off Peninsular Malaysia: up to 5 million tonnes a year, first injection as early as 2031.
cards.s: It is one of three Malaysian sites among nine projects Japan selected in 2024 for about 20 million tonnes a year. Its investment decision is still pending.
cards.d: Southern CCS Hub joint venture agreement signed 23 Oct 2026 by Petronas CCS Ventures, TotalEnergies and Mitsui: 'expected injection capacity of up to 5 million tonnes per annum' in phase 1, first injection 'as early as 2031', final investment decision pending. JOGMEC selected nine Advanced CCS Projects on 28 Jun 2024 that 'aim to store approximately 20 Mtpa of CO2 in total', five in Japan and four in the Asia-Pacific; three store off Malaysia (Northern Offshore Peninsular about 3 Mtpa, evaluated as 'promising but further initial studies were required'; Offshore Sarawak about 1.9 to 2.9 Mtpa; Southern Offshore Peninsular about 5 Mtpa). Sum about 9.9 to 10.9 Mtpa (FORA arithmetic), planned capacities, not contracts. Japan's own 2030 goal is 6 to 12 Mtpa of storage. AP's 'by 2030 ... 20 million tons' conflates the two and is not used. Kasawari CCS (3.3 Mtpa, first injection target 2027) stores domestic CO2 and is not part of the Japanese projects.
sources: METI/JOGMEC Advanced CCS Projects list, 28 Jun 2024 [S7]

cards.h: Under Malaysia's 2025 CCUS Act, once a closed offshore site's waiting period lapses, its monitoring and repair duties 'shall be transferred' to the Government.
cards.s: The operator keeps liability for its own fault. A Government fund pays the rest, fed by an injection levy that has no gazetted rate yet.
cards.d: Act 870 s. 32(1): 'Where a storage site has been closed pursuant to section 31, the obligations relating to monitoring, corrective measures and remediation measures shall be transferred to the Government'; s. 32(2): only after 'a prescribed period has lapsed from the issuance of the closure certificate' and 'other prescribed conditions' are met; s. 32(3): the transfer 'shall not include the transfer of any criminal, contractual or civil law liability ... attributable to the fault, negligence or deceit of the offshore operator'. s. 41(2): the Post-Closure Stewardship Fund consists of Government sums, the injection levy and investment income; s. 30(2)(b): the levy 'shall not be increased due to withdrawals from the Fund or risks associated with other offshore storage projects'. AGC lists show no levy order under Act 870 as at 18 Nov 2026; only P.U.(A) 346/2025 (Offshore Permit and Licensing Regulations) and the commencement notice P.U.(B) 355/2025 (in force 1 Oct 2025). The length of the prescribed period: a law firm reports the 2025 Regulations set transfer 'after at least 10 years, subject to proof of permanent CO2 containment' (regulation text not opened); a coalition of 19 groups had asked for a 200-year period. s. 19 to 20: CO2 captured abroad may be imported for permanent storage only with an import permit; the import regulations were in draft in June 2026. The Act applies to Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan only (s. 2).
sources: Carbon Capture, Utilization and Storage Act 2025 (Act 870): ss. 2, 19, 20, 30, 31, 32, 41 [S1a pp. 8, 18, 23-24, 27-28]
AGC Laws of Malaysia lists for Act 870 subsidiary legislation, checked 18 Nov 2026 [S2]

LH-AG note on P.U.(A) 346/2025, 16 Oct 2025 (reported 10-year minimum) [S10a]; GDIMY memorandum, 19 Mar 2025 (200 years) [S18b]; Ministry of Economy workshop on draft import regulations, 22 Jun 2026 [S9b]

cards.h: Under UN climate-reporting rules, Japan reports the CO2 it captures and exports. Malaysia reports any that escapes from the storage site.
cards.s: The UN climate panel's 2005 assessment put retention at very likely over 99% across 100 years for well-chosen, well-managed sites.
cards.d: 2006 IPCC Guidelines Vol 2 Ch 5 (p. 5.20): where CO2 is captured in Country A and stored in Country B, 'Country A should report the amount of CO2 captured, any emissions from transport and/or temporary storage that takes place in Country A, and the amount of CO2 exported to Country B. Country B should report the amount of CO2 imported, any emissions from transport and/or temporary storage ... and any emissions from injection and geological storage sites.' Ch 2: captured CO2 is subtracted at source and later emissions from transport, injection and the reservoir 'should be counted in national total emissions'. The 2019 Refinement made no change to Chapter 5. These are inventory-reporting rules, not liability rules. IPCC Special Report on CCS (2005) SPM: the fraction retained in appropriately selected and managed geological reservoirs is 'very likely to exceed 99% over 100 years and is likely to exceed 99% over 1,000 years'. The Ministry of Economy's '<0.001%' leakage figure attributed to the IPCC was not found in the IPCC text and is not used. Japan accepted the London Protocol's 2009 export amendment on 16 Dec 2025; Malaysia is not a party; export to a non-party needs an agreement with provisions 'at a minimum equivalent' to the Protocol.
sources: 2006 IPCC Guidelines, Vol 2 Ch 5 s. 5.10 p. 5.20 [S3a]; Ch 2 s. 2.3.4 pp. 2.36-2.37 [S3b]; 2019 Refinement Ch 5 'No Refinement' [S3c]
IPCC Special Report on Carbon Dioxide Capture and Storage (2005), SPM p. 14 [S4]
IMO status of treaties, 30 Oct 2026, pp. 399-404 [S5]; LP.3(4) amended Art. 6 [S6a]

cards.text: Carbon storage is sold as a climate service. Under Malaysia's federal law its last chapter is a public duty: a sealed reservoir the Government must watch after the operator leaves.
It is like agreeing to take back a sealed storeroom for good once the tenant moves out, before anyone has set the fee that pays for its upkeep.
sources: Act 870 s. 32 transfer; s. 30 levy with no gazetted order [S1a, S2]

cards.text: Malaysia has written the handover and left the levy rate and the Japan agreement blank. Publish both before the first tanker sails, not once the terms are a fait accompli.
sources: No levy order gazetted [S2]; bilateral agreements 'towards finalisation', unpublished [S9a]; nothing shipped [S15]

headline_suggestion: Japan plans to store 10Mt of CO2 a year off Malaysia; the deal on long-term duties is unsigned
context_suggestion: Malaysia's CCUS Act 2025 allows CO2 captured abroad to be imported for permanent storage. Japan has selected three sites off Malaysia; the bilateral agreement export requires is still being negotiated.
sources: Carbon Capture, Utilization and Storage Act 2025 (Act 870); AGC Laws of Malaysia subsidiary legislation lists (Act 870); 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories Vol 2 Ch 2 and Ch 5; 2019 Refinement; IPCC Special Report on CCS (2005) SPM; IMO Status of Treaties (30 Oct 2026); London Protocol Resolution LP.3(4) and LP.5(14); METI/JOGMEC Advanced CCS Projects (28 Jun 2024); Sarawak Environment (Reduction of Greenhouse Gases Emission) Ordinance 2023; Ministry of Economy / MyCCUS releases (2025-2026); Petronas releases (Oct 2023, Feb 2024, Oct 2025, Oct 2026); Petronas GHG data; LH-AG and Pinsent Masons notes; AP (Feb 2026); Climate Home (Mar 2025); The Star and FMT (Mar 2025)
confidence: Medium-High. HIGH on Act 870 text, AGC lists, IMO treaty status, IPCC Guidelines wording and the METI project list. MEDIUM on the post-closure period: the Act says 'a prescribed period'; the 'at least 10 years' figure comes from a law-firm summary of P.U.(A) 346/2025, whose text was not opened. MEDIUM on the Sarawak side: the 2023 Ordinance was opened, the Land (Carbon Storage) Rules 2022 were not. Planned capacities are feasibility-stage, not contracted.
needs_verification: P.U.(A) 346/2025 text: whether it sets a minimum post-closure period before s. 32 transfer ('at least 10 years' per LH-AG). Fact 2's detail carries it as reported; the card text avoids the number pending the regulation.
No injection-levy order gazetted under Act 870 s. 30 as at publication (AGC lists checked 18 Nov 2026). Fact 2 sub and the view depend on it.
Status of the Japan-Malaysia bilateral arrangement after 15 Sep 2026 ('towards finalisation'); the hook says 'unsigned'. Re-check at publication.
Southern CCS Hub JV: date 23 Oct 2026, partners, 'up to 5 Mtpa', 'as early as 2031', FID pending.
METI list: the three Malaysian project names and capacities; 'about 10 million tonnes' is the sum of planned capacities (9.9-10.9 Mtpa).

Sarawak: whether the 2023 Ordinance's CCS provisions have commenced and what the Land (Carbon Storage) Rules 2022 say on closure and transfer. The hook sub says only that Sarawak regulates the third site under its own ordinance.
source_notes: (1) Post-closure period: Act 870 says 'a prescribed period'; Pinsent Masons (on the Bill, Mar 2025) 'does not specify the duration'; LH-AG (on the Regulations, Oct 2025) 'at least 10 years'; the Economy Minister (Eco-Business paraphrase) '20 to 30 year contract'; NGOs asked for 200 years. Regulation text not opened, so the card avoids a number. (2) 'Liability' vs 'obligations': s. 32 transfers monitoring, corrective and remediation obligations and expressly excludes fault-based liability; cards use 'duties'. (3) AP's '20 million tons by 2030' conflates the nine projects' ~20 Mtpa with Japan's 2030 goal of 6-12 Mtpa; METI used. (4) Kasawari's '1% of Petronas emissions' holds only with Scope 3 included; ~6% of Scope 1+2; off cards, and Kasawari is domestic CO2. (5) Commencement: AGC gives 1 Oct 2025 (P.U.(B) 355/2025); one law-firm note says 1 Aug 2025 (publication date). AGC used. (6) Jurisdiction off Sarawak is before the Federal Court (25-29 Jan 2027); cards state what each law says about its own scope and take no side.
guardrails_applied: Nothing presented as shipped, signed or operating beyond what is: 'No tonne has shipped', 'unsigned', 'investment decision pending', 'as early as 2031'.
Statute's word 'obligations'/'duties' used, and s. 32(3) fault-liability carve-out stated on fact 2.
Sarawak project not placed under Act 870; hook sub states each law's own scope; no position on the Federal Court dispute.
IPCC rule described as reporting, with the 99% retention estimate on the same card so leak risk is not overstated.
'Carbon colonialism' and 'dumping ground' not used as FORA's words.
No cost-to-taxpayer figure; levy described only as unset.
Elevated word 'fait accompli' in the view; 'amanah' avoided for its party-name collision.
